h: Climbing Culture and Steel City Extras
p: Sheffield has deep roots in climbing, thanks to the gritstone edges of the Peak District right on its doorstep. Stanage Edge and Burbage are famous with climbers from all over the country, and an obstacle course is a fun, low-pressure way for kids to discover whether that sort of activity might be for them.

Obstacle training also builds the same things climbers need: grip strength, body control and the confidence to commit to a move. If your youngsters love it, the city's many indoor climbing walls are a natural next step.

Back in town, Kelham Island Museum tells Sheffield's steel-making story, complete with a mighty working steam engine. Weston Park Museum, by the university, is free and great for families, with natural history, archaeology and local stories under one roof. The Sheffield Botanical Gardens offer glass pavilions and peaceful lawns, while Graves Park in the south of the city has woodland, ponds and an animal farm that little ones love.

If the weather's fine, Padley Gorge in the Peak District is a classic family walk, with a stream to paddle in, mossy boulders to scramble over and woodland that feels like something out of a storybook. Pack a picnic and you've got the perfect calmer half to a ninja day.
